articles.title: Scientists discover the hidden “muscles” trees use to straighten themselves
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that trees can sense their own shape and straighten their trunks using specialized wood that acts like opposing muscles. This remarkable ability helps trees maintain their posture and could lead to stronger forests, better timber, and more resilient crops.
articles.content:
Trees have a remarkable ability to sense their own shape and adjust their growth to stay upright. This awareness of body position, known as proprioception, was once thought to exist only in animals. However, in 2012, researchers working with INRAE demonstrated that plants also possess this ability (Bastien R. et al., PNAS).

This internal sense allows plants to monitor their posture and make adjustments that help them grow as straight as possible (Moulia et al., Science). Although scientists had established that plants could detect their own shape, the biological processes responsible for turning that information into physical movement remained a mystery.

How Scientists Isolated Trees' Hidden Sense

Plants use several kinds of information to guide their growth. They respond to gravity, detect the direction of sunlight, and monitor the shape and position of their own stems. To understand how this internal sense works independently, researchers needed to eliminate the directional signals provided by gravity and light.

They developed an unusual experimental system designed to isolate proprioception. Young trees were placed on a horizontal platform that rotated around its axis inside a sphere illuminated equally from every direction. The rotating platform prevented the trees from receiving a consistent directional signal from gravity, while the surrounding light eliminated cues about which way they should grow.

This arrangement allowed the researchers to investigate how trees respond to their own shape without relying on the usual environmental signals that influence their growth.

The Muscle-Like Wood That Helps Trees Straighten Themselves

The experiment began with young poplar trees positioned horizontally. As the trees grew, their stems gradually curved upward, bringing their tops back toward a vertical position.

This response depends on a specialized type of wood called tension wood. Unlike ordinary wood, tension wood can generate pulling forces as it develops. When it forms along the upper side of a stem, it acts much like a contracting muscle, pulling the stem upward and causing it to bend.

After approximately ten days, once the trees had developed a noticeable curve, researchers moved them into the experimental apparatus. Over the following weeks, something remarkable happened. Instead of maintaining their curved shapes, the stems slowly straightened until they became nearly straight again.

To determine what caused this change, the team examined the structure of the wood that developed during the straightening process.

They found that the original tension wood, which had formed along the upper side of the stems and pulled them upward, stopped developing once the experimental system was activated. At the same time, identical tension wood began forming on the opposite side.

This newly formed wood appeared to act like an opposing muscle, producing a pulling force in the other direction. As the forces worked against each other, the curved stems gradually returned to a straight shape.

The production of tension wood involves a complex sequence of biological events controlled at the cellular level. The findings indicate that a tree's internal sense of its own shape helps regulate this process, determining where tension wood develops to correct its posture.

A Surprising Discovery About How Trees Control Their Shape

Previously, scientists believed that tension wood formed only on the upper side of stems, where it helped pull them upward. This is particularly noticeable near the bases of trees growing on mountain slopes, where trunks often need to curve to maintain an upright position.

The new research reveals that tension wood has a more versatile role. It can develop on opposing sides of a stem and generate forces in different directions, functioning much like the opposing muscle groups animals use to maintain posture and control movement.

This discovery suggests that trees possess a sophisticated system for coordinating their growth. They combine information about their surroundings (such as light and gravity) with an internal awareness of their own shape. By processing these signals, they can regulate where tension wood develops and adjust their posture accordingly.

Why This Discovery Matters for Forests and Agriculture

The ability to sense and correct their own shape is especially important when trees encounter environmental disturbances. Powerful storms, landslides, and other extreme events can bend or displace trees, making the capacity to regain an appropriate posture essential for their resilience.

Understanding this mechanism could become increasingly valuable as climate change exposes forests to more extreme conditions.

The findings also have practical implications for forestry and agriculture. By identifying plants with particularly effective proprioception, scientists may be able to select varieties that grow straighter, maintain better posture, and produce higher-quality wood.

In agriculture, the same knowledge could help researchers develop cereal crops that are less likely to fall over before harvest. This problem, known as lodging, can cause significant yield losses when crops collapse toward the end of the growing season.

The discovery could also improve timber quality. Poorly coordinated tension wood formation can create excessive internal stresses in trees, potentially affecting the properties of the wood they produce.

Bruno Moulia, INRAE research director, explained:

"What we have uncovered is a genuine sensorimotor loop operating in the woody parts of trees! Poor coordination in the successive activation of tension wood results in excessive internal tension, which can affect wood quality. These findings therefore reshape more applied research aimed at improving wood quality... and at obtaining trees that are as straight and as relaxed as possible, whatever life throws at them!"

The research also highlights the importance of combining expertise from different scientific fields to understand the complex ways plants interact with their environment.

Félix Hartman, INRAE research engineer, emphasized the collaborative effort behind the discovery:

"Revealing the remarkable capabilities of trees requires a great deal of ingenuity. In this project, we achieved it by bringing together researchers from different disciplines, with complementary skills and perspectives. This requires time and perseverance, but these interdisciplinary discoveries show that the effort is worthwhile."
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant scientific discovery about trees' proprioception and their ability to straighten themselves using specialized tension wood acting like muscles. This finding has broad implications for forest resilience, timber quality, and agriculture, especially in the context of climate change. The story is focused, detailed, and highlights a breakthrough with tangible benefits for ecosystems and human industries.
articles.personality_title: Scientists uncover how trees straighten themselves using muscle-like wood
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Trees have long been known to grow upright, but how they sense and correct their shape was unclear. While animals have a sense called proprioception to know their body position, scientists only recently discovered that plants have a similar ability. In 2012, researchers showed plants can sense their own shape, but the exact way trees adjust their trunks remained a mystery.

**What happened** – Researchers at INRAE conducted an experiment with young poplar trees placed horizontally on a rotating platform inside a sphere lit equally from all sides. This setup removed normal signals from gravity and light, isolating the trees’ own sensing ability. Over weeks, the curved stems of the trees slowly straightened. Scientists found this was due to special wood called tension wood forming on opposite sides of the stem, acting like opposing muscles that pull the trunk straight.

**Impact** – This discovery shows trees actively control their posture using tension wood that contracts like muscles. It changes the previous belief that tension wood only forms on one side to pull upward. Understanding this “muscle-like” wood helps explain how trees recover after storms or bends caused by nature. It also opens possibilities to grow straighter trees for stronger forests and better timber, and to improve crops by selecting plants that stand firm and resist falling over.

**What's next step** – Scientists hope to use this knowledge to breed or engineer trees and crops with better posture control. This could lead to forests more resilient to climate change and crops that produce higher yields by avoiding lodging, when plants fall before harvest. Further research will explore how to apply these findings in forestry and agriculture for practical benefits.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Trees use special tension wood that works like muscles to sense and straighten their trunks, a discovery that could improve forest health and crop strength in changing environments.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des scientifiques découvrent comment les arbres se redressent grâce à un bois semblable à des muscles
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – On sait depuis longtemps que les arbres poussent droit, mais on ne comprenait pas comment ils sentent et corrigent leur forme. Les animaux possèdent une capacité appelée proprioception pour connaître la position de leur corps, et en 2012, des chercheurs ont montré que les plantes ont aussi cette capacité. Cependant, la manière dont les arbres ajustent leurs troncs restait inconnue.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Des chercheurs d’INRAE ont mené une expérience avec de jeunes peupliers placés horizontalement sur une plateforme tournante dans une sphère éclairée de manière uniforme. Ce dispositif éliminait les signaux habituels de la gravité et de la lumière, isolant la capacité de perception propre des arbres. Au fil des semaines, les troncs courbés se sont redressés lentement. Les scientifiques ont découvert que cela était dû à un bois spécial appelé bois de tension qui se forme de part et d’autre du tronc, agissant comme des muscles opposés tirant pour redresser l’arbre.

**Impact** – Cette découverte montre que les arbres contrôlent activement leur posture grâce à ce bois de tension qui fonctionne comme un muscle. Elle change l’idée précédente selon laquelle ce bois ne se formait que d’un côté pour tirer vers le haut. Comprendre ce bois « musculaire » explique comment les arbres récupèrent après des tempêtes ou des déformations naturelles. Cela ouvre aussi la voie à des arbres plus droits pour des forêts plus solides et un meilleur bois, ainsi qu’à des cultures résistantes qui tiennent debout.

**Prochaine étape** – Les scientifiques souhaitent utiliser cette connaissance pour sélectionner ou modifier des arbres et des plantes cultivées capables de mieux contrôler leur posture. Cela pourrait rendre les forêts plus résistantes au changement climatique et augmenter les rendements agricoles en évitant que les plantes ne s’effondrent avant la récolte. D’autres recherches viseront à appliquer ces résultats en foresterie et agriculture.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Les arbres utilisent un bois de tension spécial qui agit comme des muscles pour sentir et redresser leur tronc, une découverte qui pourrait améliorer la santé des forêts et la solidité des cultures face aux changements environnementaux.
articles.personality_title_es: Científicos descubren cómo los árboles se enderezan usando madera similar a músculos
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Se sabe que los árboles crecen derechos, pero no se entendía cómo sienten y corrigen su forma. Los animales tienen una capacidad llamada propiocepción para conocer la posición de su cuerpo, y en 2012 se demostró que las plantas también la poseen. Sin embargo, cómo los árboles ajustan sus troncos seguía siendo un misterio.

**Qué pasó** – Investigadores de INRAE hicieron un experimento con álamos jóvenes colocados horizontalmente en una plataforma giratoria dentro de una esfera iluminada uniformemente. Esto eliminó las señales normales de gravedad y luz, aislando la capacidad de los árboles para sentir su forma. Con el tiempo, los troncos curvados se enderezaron lentamente. Descubrieron que esto se debía a un tipo especial de madera llamada madera de tensión que se forma en lados opuestos del tronco, actuando como músculos que tiran para enderezarlo.

**Impacto** – Este hallazgo muestra que los árboles controlan activamente su postura usando madera de tensión que funciona como un músculo. Cambia la idea anterior de que esta madera solo se formaba en un lado para tirar hacia arriba. Entender esta madera «muscular» explica cómo los árboles se recuperan tras tormentas o daños naturales. También abre la posibilidad de cultivar árboles más rectos para bosques más fuertes y mejor madera, y mejorar cultivos para que se mantengan firmes.

**Próximo paso** – Los científicos esperan usar este conocimiento para criar o modificar árboles y cultivos que controlen mejor su postura. Esto podría hacer que los bosques sean más resistentes al cambio climático y aumentar la producción agrícola evitando que las plantas se caigan antes de la cosecha. Se realizarán más estudios para aplicar estos hallazgos en la silvicultura y agricultura.

**Resumen en una frase** – Los árboles usan madera de tensión especial que actúa como músculos para sentir y enderezar sus troncos, un descubrimiento que podría mejorar la salud de los bosques y la fortaleza de los cultivos en entornos cambiantes.

articles.title: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
articles.summary: It was feared The Short-Necked Oil Beetle had become extinct in Wales after recent surveys
articles.content:
Last year, the survey at Castlemartin found only dead adults of this particular beetle, raising concerns about the future of this species and its continued presence on the site.

But this year, after three years of searching, experts discovered larvae of the beetle on a small area of the site, suggesting that surveyors had managed to find some of the hatchlings from a larger batch of immature beetles.

The number and distribution of the beetle larvae seen also supported this, according to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).

The Short-Necked Oil Beetle is classed as nationally rare within Great Britain and listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, external.

They can typically be found from March to June in flower-rich coastal grassland and sand dune habitat, and are most active on warm, sunny days.

Adults can grow up toe 24mm (0.9in) in length and the life span of an adult is approximately one year.

NRW said these conditions mean there are only a handful of suitable sites in the UK.

They were rediscovered in Devon in 2006 and on the Isle of Coll, in Scotland, in 2009. Since then, populations have been found on Tiree, Islay, Barra and Uist.

Castlemartin Range, in Pembrokeshire, is currently the only place in Wales where the species can be found and it is being consistently surveyed by conservationists.

The project is part of Wales's "flagship species recovery programme", said NRW, which works to conserve the Short-Necked Oil Beetle Sand other species that share similar habitats.

Hobbs described the Short-Necked Oil Beetle as an "amazing creature" and said their work needed to consider the "needs of several species to be effective".

She thanked their partners and volunteers for their continued support, despite having two years without a larval sighting.

"We look forward to the continued management of the site so that this amazing species can survive now and into the future."
articles.reasoning: The rediscovery of the rare Short-Necked Oil Beetle larvae in Wales after fears of extinction represents a significant conservation success with positive implications for biodiversity and habitat preservation. The story focuses on a single species and details ongoing conservation efforts, indicating meaningful real-world environmental impact.

articles.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
articles.summary: Countries have been trying to get a global agreement to halt nature decline back on track.
articles.content:
In Armenia's capital this week a fight between politicians broke out - not the mass brawl in its parliament that was so widely documented on social media - but between delegates from nearly 200 countries.

The world's nations have been gathered in Yerevan for nearly two weeks negotiating, and arguing, over a new agreement on nature.

Early on Saturday morning, hours after talks were due to finish, they finally agreed the key parts of a new action plan.

"And that's it. Perfect," said the meeting president, Hambardzum Matevosyan.

Four years earlier the same countries had signed a landmark deal committing to "halt and reverse" the decline of nature.

That global deal in 2022 - the Global Biodiversity Framework - contained 24 targets including putting 30% of the world's land and seas into protection by the end of the decade.

They agreed that action was urgent.

The world is currently in a sixth mass extinction event with species becoming extinct at 100 times the natural rate because of human activities, scientists say.

But according to the UN this week,, external the world is on track to achieve just one of those two dozen targets.

As part of this week's deal, countries acknowledged they were falling behind.

"While not particularly exciting or detailed, it's good news that countries could reach agreement," said Catherine Weller, from environmental charity Fauna & Flora.

"We cannot just plod on to 2030 without a course correction; nature is critical to all life on Earth: to our economies, to our wellbeing," she added.

This was echoed by Craig Bennett, CEO of The Wildlife Trusts, who told BBC News: "We are still seeing an appalling loss, threatening the collapse of ecosystems globally. We run out of words really about how serious this is."

But he added "the better news is there are so many examples worldwide about how... to turn things around".

Countries have put 623 million acres (252m hectares) of degraded land into protection, external - an area bigger than Greenland.

Just last month the WWF praised conservation efforts which had achieved the recovery of key species including elephants, green sea turtles and tigers.

Countries have recognised the main barrier to accelerating those efforts is money.

In 2022, they agreed they would put $30bn (£22.4bn) towards nature recovery efforts by the end of the decade, and mobilise a further $170bn from private sources.

But years later many nations have been redirecting international aid to defence budgets and to deal with repeated energy shocks, such that pledges are not at the rate required to reach those targets, according to the UN. , external

At this meeting, more than $1bn was pledged, with half of that coming from philanthropists including Leonardo DiCaprio's Re:wild organisation.
articles.reasoning: The article reports on a significant global agreement among nearly 200 countries to address nature decline and biodiversity loss, acknowledging the urgency and setting targets for conservation. Despite challenges with funding and progress, the deal represents meaningful international cooperation with tangible conservation efforts already underway, such as protecting large land areas and species recovery. This has broad environmental and societal impact, making it genuinely inspiring good news.
articles.personality_title: Nearly 200 countries agree on new plan to protect nature
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – For years, nearly 200 countries have been trying to stop the loss of nature and protect the Earth’s plants and animals. In 2022, they made a big promise to save 30% of land and seas by 2030, but progress has been slow.

**What happened** – In June 2024, these countries met in Yerevan, Armenia, to discuss a new plan. After nearly two weeks of talks, they agreed on key parts of an action plan to help nature. This happened just hours after the meeting was supposed to end.

**Impact** – This agreement shows that countries recognize the urgent need to protect nature. Scientists warn that many species are disappearing much faster than normal. Although only one of the 24 targets from the 2022 deal is on track, countries have already protected large areas of land—bigger than Greenland—and helped some animals like elephants and turtles recover.

**What’s next step** – The big challenge is money. Countries promised to spend $30 billion by 2030 and get more funds from private groups. At the meeting, over $1 billion was pledged, including donations from celebrities like Leonardo DiCaprio. The hope is that this funding will speed up efforts to meet the nature protection goals.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Nearly 200 countries agreed on a new plan to protect nature, with some progress made and new funding pledged to help reach important conservation goals by 2030.
articles.personality_title_fr: Près de 200 pays s’accordent sur un nouveau plan pour protéger la nature
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Depuis plusieurs années, près de 200 pays essaient d’arrêter la perte de la nature et de protéger les plantes et les animaux de la Terre. En 2022, ils ont fait une grande promesse de sauvegarder 30 % des terres et des mers d’ici 2030, mais les progrès sont lents.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – En juin 2024, ces pays se sont réunis à Erevan, en Arménie, pour discuter d’un nouveau plan. Après presque deux semaines de négociations, ils ont accepté les points clés d’un plan d’action pour aider la nature, juste quelques heures avant la fin prévue de la réunion.

**Impact** – Cet accord montre que les pays reconnaissent l’urgence de protéger la nature. Les scientifiques alertent sur la disparition rapide de nombreuses espèces. Bien qu’un seul des 24 objectifs de 2022 soit en bonne voie, des zones protégées plus grandes que le Groenland ont déjà été créées, et certains animaux comme les éléphants et les tortues ont commencé à se rétablir.

**Prochaine étape** – Le grand défi reste l’argent. Les pays ont promis de dépenser 30 milliards de dollars d’ici 2030 et d’obtenir des fonds privés. Lors de la réunion, plus d’un milliard de dollars ont été promis, y compris des dons de célébrités comme Leonardo DiCaprio. L’espoir est que cet argent accélère les efforts pour atteindre les objectifs de protection.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Près de 200 pays ont accepté un nouveau plan pour protéger la nature, avec des progrès déjà réalisés et de nouveaux financements promis pour atteindre les objectifs importants d’ici 2030.
articles.personality_title_es: Casi 200 países acuerdan un nuevo plan para proteger la naturaleza
articles.personality_presentation_es:

**Próximo paso** – El gran reto es el dinero. Los países prometieron gastar 30 mil millones de dólares para 2030 y conseguir más fondos de grupos privados. **Frase clave** – Casi 200 países acordaron un nuevo plan para proteger la naturaleza, con algunos avances y nuevos fondos prometidos para ayudar a alcanzar importantes objetivos de conservación para 2030.

articles.title: Rhino siblings celebrate first birthday with cake
articles.summary: Markus and Mo weighed about 70kg (11st) at birth, and now weigh about 500kg (78st) each.
articles.content:
Two rhino calves have celebrated their first birthday with cakes made of pellets, carrots and salad leaves.

Siblings Markus and Mo were born at Cotswold Wildlife Park, near Burford, last year.

The pair weighed about 70kg (11st) at birth, and now weigh about 500kg (78st) each. Their arrival took the number of rhinos at the park to nine, the most in its 56-year history.

White rhinos were close to extinction in the early 1900s, with fewer than 50 thought to remain in Africa. They are now the most numerous of the five rhino species, but the park says conservation remains vital.
articles.reasoning: The article highlights the successful birth and growth of two rhino calves at a wildlife park, symbolizing positive progress in rhino conservation. It emphasizes the importance of ongoing conservation efforts for a species once near extinction, which has broad environmental and ecological significance.
articles.personality_title: Rhino siblings mark first birthday with special cake at wildlife park
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – White rhinos were almost extinct in the early 1900s, with fewer than 50 left in Africa. Conservation efforts have helped increase their numbers, but protecting them remains important.

**What happened** – Two rhino siblings named Markus and Mo celebrated their first birthday at Cotswold Wildlife Park near Burford. They enjoyed cakes made from pellets, carrots, and salad leaves. When born, each calf weighed about 70 kilograms (11 stone), and now they weigh around 500 kilograms (78 stone) each.

**Impact** – Their birth brought the total number of rhinos at the park to nine, the highest in the park’s 56-year history. This shows progress in caring for and growing the rhino population, which is important because white rhinos were once very close to disappearing.

**What's next step** – The park will continue to care for Markus, Mo, and the other rhinos while supporting conservation efforts. This helps protect rhinos and teaches visitors about why these animals need to be saved.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Two young rhinos at a wildlife park celebrated their first birthday, showing positive growth in efforts to protect a species that once faced extinction.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des frères rhinocéros fêtent leur premier anniversaire avec un gâteau spécial au parc animalier
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les rhinocéros blancs étaient presque éteints au début des années 1900, avec moins de 50 individus en Afrique. Les efforts de conservation ont aidé à augmenter leur nombre, mais leur protection reste essentielle.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Deux frères rhinocéros, Markus et Mo, ont célébré leur premier anniversaire au parc animalier de Cotswold près de Burford. Ils ont dégusté des gâteaux faits de granulés, de carottes et de feuilles de salade. À la naissance, chaque petit pesait environ 70 kilogrammes, et ils pèsent maintenant environ 500 kilogrammes chacun.

**Impact** – Leur naissance a porté le nombre total de rhinocéros au parc à neuf, un record dans les 56 ans d’existence du parc. Cela montre des progrès dans la protection et la croissance de la population de rhinocéros, importante car les rhinocéros blancs étaient autrefois proches de la disparition.

**Prochaine étape** – Le parc continuera à s’occuper de Markus, Mo et des autres rhinocéros tout en soutenant les efforts de conservation. Cela aide à protéger les rhinocéros et à sensibiliser les visiteurs à l’importance de sauver ces animaux.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Deux jeunes rhinocéros ont fêté leur premier anniversaire dans un parc animalier, illustrant les progrès positifs pour protéger une espèce autrefois en voie d’extinction.
articles.personality_title_es: Cachorros de rinoceronte celebran su primer cumpleaños con un pastel especial en parque de vida silvestre
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los rinocerontes blancos estuvieron casi extinguidos a principios del siglo XX, con menos de 50 en África. Los esfuerzos de conservación han ayudado a aumentar su número, pero protegerlos sigue siendo importante.

**Qué pasó** – Dos hermanos rinocerontes, Markus y Mo, celebraron su primer cumpleaños en el Parque de Vida Silvestre de Cotswold, cerca de Burford. Disfrutaron de pasteles hechos con pellets, zanahorias y hojas de lechuga. Al nacer, cada uno pesaba unos 70 kilogramos, y ahora pesan alrededor de 500 kilogramos cada uno.

**Impacto** – Su nacimiento llevó el total de rinocerontes en el parque a nueve, el número más alto en los 56 años de historia del parque. Esto muestra avances en el cuidado y aumento de la población de rinocerontes, importante porque los rinocerontes blancos estuvieron cerca de desaparecer.

**Próximo paso** – El parque seguirá cuidando a Markus, Mo y a los otros rinocerontes mientras apoya los esfuerzos de conservación. Esto ayuda a proteger a los rinocerontes y a educar a los visitantes sobre la importancia de salvar a estos animales.

**Resumen en una frase** – Dos jóvenes rinocerontes en un parque de vida silvestre celebraron su primer cumpleaños, mostrando un progreso positivo en la protección de una especie que estuvo al borde de la extinción.
